questions.q: What does 'build once, promote the same artifact' mean?
options: Retrain the model separately in each environment
Staging and production run the same model file and differ only in configuration
Only build the model on Fridays
Use a different model file for each customer
questions.explain: If production received a freshly trained model, what you tested in staging would not be what is live.

questions.q: Why does the registry record a SHA-256 hash when a model version is registered?
options: To make the file smaller
To encrypt the model for customers
To choose the model's learning rate
To detect if the file changed between registration and promotion
questions.explain: In the lesson, swapping the model file after staging made the hash check fail, and promotion was refused.

questions.q: In the lesson, version 2 was refused when sent straight to production. Why?
options: Promotion rules require a model to be in staging before production
Version 2 had a lower AUC than production
Production only accepts version 1
There was no config file
questions.explain: The registry enforces stage order so a model cannot skip staging.

questions.q: Why is rolling back in this design fast?
options: Because the old model is retrained from scratch in seconds
Because production is an alias that can be repointed to the saved previous version
Because customers do not notice rollbacks
Because rollbacks skip the audit log
questions.explain: The previous production version is stored, so rollback is just moving the pointer back; no retraining or rebuild is needed.

questions.q: Which of these did the lesson say a GitHub environment can do, as of this writing?
options: Automatically fix failing tests
Train the model for you
Require reviewer approval and hold secrets available only to jobs that use it
Replace the model registry entirely
questions.explain: Environments can require reviewers, add wait timers, restrict deployment branches, and store environment-specific secrets. Check current docs, as availability depends on plan.
